_about: Defaults for each supplier. To change them without a new version of the add-on, put your changes in suppliers.json in the add-on's own folder in Home Assistant (/addon_configs/<this add-on>/, over Samba or the File editor): the same layout, only what's different (a supplier with the same name has those fields changed; a new name is added). It's read again within a few minutes of changing.
Anything set on the web page (Settings > Your supplier) still wins over these.
name: shown on the page, and how a supplier is matched in the other settings.

type: how its integration shows the plan in Home Assistant: kraken (a dispatching binary sensor and a ready time entity, Octopus Energy and EDF Energy) or schedule_sensor (a sensor with a schedule attribute, E.ON Next); src/supplier_types/ has one file for each.
integration: its Home Assistant integration's domain, so the add-on notices when it's updated (Diagnostics > Health).
colour: its colour on the page (#rrggbb).

dispatch_prefix: the start of its smart charging (intelligent dispatching) binary sensor's entity ID. With it: dispatch_suffix (the end of that entity ID, default dispatching), ready_entity_suffix (what replaces it for the ready time entity, a time. or select. one: default target_time), planned_attribute and completed_attribute (the sensor's attributes listing the slots: default planned_dispatches and completed_dispatches).
schedule_sensor_suffix: instead, a sensor whose entity ID contains this, with the slots in schedule_attribute (default schedule) (E.ON Next).
slot_fields: the names of each slot's fields: start, end, kwh (the energy) and source (default start, end, charge_in_kwh, source).
calendar_words: words in its saving sessions calendar's ID or name that say it's this supplier's.
ready_times: the ready (target) times its app accepts, from / to on the hour or half hour; null: it has no ready time.
daily_limit_h: the most hours of smart charging it schedules (Force schedule on supplier keeps within it); null: no limit.
limit_reset: when that limit starts again: a time (HH:MM, every day), or "rolling" (any 24 hours).
other: used for a supplier that isn't listed.
saving_sessions: words (in a calendar's ID or name) that mean saving sessions, not_words that mean the opposite (e.g. Power Up), and prefer: picked first when several are found.
